AccountPatchBody.description:
PATCH body: like `AccountBody`, plus an explicit way to empty a stored secret (same
semantics as `clearSecrets` in PATCH /api/settings). A blank `secret` alone still means
"unchanged".
AccountPatchBody.title: AccountPatchBody

SystemWrite.description:
Hand-maintainable device fields only (POST/PATCH /api/systems).

System fields (status, lastSeen, openPorts, discoveryKey, extra, ...) belong to scan/monitor and
are silently ignored (`extra="ignore"`, so older clients that send the whole device keep
working). The handlers pass only `exclude_unset` values on, so a save never writes back stale
copies of fields the client did not change.
SystemWrite.title: SystemWrite

post.description:
Stores what the first-run wizard collected. Each system with a password gets a matching
account row, so the credential lands encrypted rather than in a free-text note.

Runs once: afterwards 409 (auth and validation come first). No `await` between the check and
the write, so concurrent calls cannot both pass. A device whose IP matches exactly one
existing non-container row updates that row instead of adding a duplicate.

post.description:
The only way a second factor comes off an account -- see the module note above the TOTP
routes. Clears it rather than disabling the requirement: `current_user` treats
`totpEnabled = False` as "must enroll again", so this recovers a locked-out user (lost
phone, reinstalled app). All sessions of the target end, without exception (also when an admin
resets their own factor): an open session could otherwise enroll a factor of its own, which
would hand whoever only knew the password a second factor. Same as the CLI.
